body: Recurrent-depth language models improve inference-time reasoning by repeatedly applying a shared network to refine internal representations, but the additional recurrent computation also increases inference cost. This overhead is particularly pronounced during long-context prefill, where the full input sequence is repeatedly processed across recurrent depth. Weight-and-activation quantization offers a natural way to accelerate this computation through lower-precision arithmetic, yet repeatedly applying quantized computation introduces numerical perturbations that accumulate along the recurrent trajectory. We systematically analyze how such errors propagate across recurrent depth and show that quantization errors introduced earlier are attenuated by more subsequent recurrent steps and therefore have a smaller effect on the final representation. Matched-budget experiments strongly support this prediction, showing that placing quantized computation earlier in recurrent depth consistently yields the best fidelity. Based on this insight, we introduce RAMP (Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision), which performs early recurrent refinement using low-precision weight-and-activation computation and restores high precision for terminal refinement. Across context lengths up to 4K, RAMP preserves near-full-precision prefill quality while achieving up to 1.16x end-to-end first-prefill speedup on an NVIDIA H100, corresponding to a 13.9% latency reduction.
summaryZh: 该研究针对循环深度语言模型在长上下文预填充（prefill）阶段的计算开销问题，提出了一种名为RAMP（Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision）的技术。RAMP通过分析量化误差沿循环深度的传播规律，将低精度计算应用于早期循环层以加速，并将高精度计算保留用于最终的精炼。实验表明，RAMP在保持近乎全精度预填充质量的同时，在NVIDIA H100上实现了高达1.16倍的端到端预填充加速，降低了13.9%的延迟。
